One dry season, the Rain spoke: "River, I will give you my waters. All that I have, I offer freely."

The River was suspicious. "Why would you give without asking return?"

"Because," said the Rain, "what I give to you returns to me threefold. You carry my gift to the ocean, the ocean sends it skyward, and I am replenished to give again."

But the River, scarred by a drought when mountain snows had betrayed him, held back. "I will accept only a little," he said. "I cannot trust such generosity."

So the Rain gave sparingly in return, and the River ran shallow. The fields withered. The people thirred.

Seeing the suffering, both finally understood: trust was not weakness but creation itself. The Rain poured freely, the River received openly, and the cycle flourished.

Now when Rain falls, the River runs deep and full, knowing that what flows away returns transformed—not as loss, but as abundance multiplied.

*The measure of what we give determines what we receive.*
